summary: Rebuilt content/blog/25-utility-bill-taxes-fees-franchise-charges-explained.md from 467 procedural words to 984 words (target 700–1,000) with fetch-verified jurisdiction examples replacing the 'check your bill and tariff' filler. All five mission elements delivered: three-charge Quick Answer, 'What Each One Looks Like on a Bill' table with named/published rates, gross-receipts explanation answering why tax hit delivery charges, preserved-and-upgraded verify workflow, and 6 Q&A FAQs. Site builds cleanly in Hugo; zero unsourced numbers remain.
findings: Every number in the new body traces to a page fetched this run (retrieved 2026-08-29): Pasadena UUT rates (electricity 7.67%, gas 7.9%, water 7.67%), RCW 35.21.870's 6% cap on WA city utility taxes, Cheney WA's voter-approved 14.75% total, FL Stat. 166.231's 10% municipal public-service-tax cap, MN Stat. 216B.36's gross-receipts franchise-fee basis, and LA's Lifeline-page proof that the UUT appears as a 'Los Angeles City Tax' line on real DWP bills

No fetchable franchise-fee percentage could be verified despite ~10 attempts (KCMO/Municode/Portland/SMUD/CPS/Minneapolis/Austin/Seattle all 403/404/JS-shells; search engines returned dictionary noise; DDG/Bing throttled). Per mission instruction, I used MN 216B.36's verified gross-operating-revenues basis with NO dollar figure rather than inventing a 'typical' percent

Search-engine degradation was the run's main obstacle: web_search and Bing keyed on dictionary headwords ('utility', 'los', 'riverside', '21'); the workarounds that succeeded were direct gov-URL fetches, link-grepping site navigation, statute-publisher fetches (app.leg.wa.gov, leg.state.fl.us, revisor.mn.gov all served clean static HTML), and DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint for the two leads it landed (MRSC, KCMO)

Sibling 19 was rebuilt in parallel this run with the same evidence-bar style (bracketed source markers, retrieved-dates in sources frontmatter, named-rate tables) — my page matches its conventions, links it twice, and contains zero rider/surcharge content duplication

MRSC's gross-receipts mechanics ($100 bill → $11.11 tax at a 10% stated rate; tax-on-revenue-including-the-tax) directly answers the mission's 'why is tax charged on delivery too' question with a sourced general answer

The two old DOE sources carried no numbers in the old body and were dropped; the old 5-H2 procedural workflow survives compressed inside 'How to Read Yours' (verify against tariff/ordinance is now step 2–4)
